pr.title: coverage: Only merge adjacent coverage spans
pr.description:
For a long time, coverage instrumentation has automatically “merged” spans with the same control-flow into a smaller number of larger spans, even when the spans being merged are not overlapping or adjacent. This causes any source text between the original spans to be included in the merged span, which is then associated with an execution count when shown in coverage reports.

That approach causes a number of problems:
- The intervening source text can contain all sorts of things that shouldn't really be marked as executable code (e.g. nested items, parts of macro invocations, long comments). In some cases we have complicated workarounds (e.g. bucketing to avoid merging spans across nested items), but in other cases there isn't much we can do.
- Merging can have aesthetically weird effects, such as including unbalanced parentheses, because the merging process doesn't really understand what it's doing at a source code level.
- It generally leads to an accumulation of piled-on heuristics and special cases that give decent-looking results, but are fiendishly difficult to modify or replace.

Therefore, this PR aims to abolish the merging of non-adjacent coverage spans.

The big tradeoff here is that the resulting coverage metadata (embedded in the instrumented binary) tends to become larger, because the overall number of distinct spans has increased. That's unfortunate, but I see it as the inevitable cost of cleaning up the messes and inaccuracies that were caused by the old approach. And the resulting spans do tend to be more accurate to the program's actual control-flow.

---

The `.coverage` snapshot changes give an indication of how this PR will affect user-visible coverage reports. In many cases the changes to reporting are minor or even nonexistent, despite substantial changes to the metadata (as indicated by `.cov-map` snapshots).

---

try-job: aarch64-gnu
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: InstrumentCoverage extracted HIR/MIR coverage spans, optionally used a function-signature span extended to the start of the body, processed holes by splitting covspans into buckets, removed unwanted overlaps, and then merged sorted Covspan entries in each bucket. The historical merge logic merged whenever the BCB matched, even with a source gap: `if self.bcb != other.bcb { return false; } self.span = self.span.to(other.span); true`. The old documentation explicitly allowed this: `Note that compatible covspans can be merged even if their underlying spans are not overlapping/adjacent; any space between them will also be part of the merged covspan.` The HIR signature logic also widened the signature span with `.map(|fn_sig_span| fn_sig_span.with_hi(body_span.lo()));`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically incorrect transformation: given two same-BCB coverage spans A and B where A.hi < B.lo and the gap is non-empty, InstrumentCoverage emitted one merged mapping spanning A.lo through B.hi, thereby attributing the intervening comments, whitespace, macro text, nested items, or other holes to the same execution count. Separately, it transformed a function signature span ending before the body start into `[fn_sig.lo, body.lo)`, pulling the signature-to-body gap into the signature mapping. The corrected invariant is: two covspans may be merged only if `(a.bcb == b.bcb) && a.span.overlaps_or_adjacent(b.span)`; the function signature span is used as-is, not extended to `body_span.lo()`. The PR states: `Therefore, this PR aims to abolish the merging of non-adjacent coverage spans.`
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with coverage instrumentation where extracted coverage spans share a BCB but are separated by source that is not itself represented by an adjacent coverage span (blank lines/comments, macro invocations, nested items, attributes, async/closure desugarings, or hole regions), and/or where the function signature span ends before the body span. The relevant pass input is sorted HIR/MIR coverage spans plus merged hole spans; the pass output is `CodeMapping { span, bcb }` metadata. The input domain is not ordinary control-flow correctness; it is source-span attribution for coverage reports.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage must not merge same-BCB coverage spans across non-adjacent source gaps or extend the function-signature span to the body start. Merge only overlapping or adjacent spans, so intervening non-code text and holes are not credited with an execution count.
analysis.trigger: A coverage-instrumented Rust function has two extracted covspans with the same BCB but a non-empty source gap between them, or has a function signature span ending before the body start. In those cases the old code emitted a single oversized mapping (or widened the signature mapping) instead of preserving separate spans.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the crate, so InstrumentCoverage extracts coverage spans and holes from HIR/MIR.
The candidate covspans are sorted and share the same BCB.
The candidate spans are not overlapping or adjacent; source text or a hole lies between them.
For the signature case, the function signature span has the same context and filename as the body and precedes it.
pitfalls: Do not merge solely on equal BCB; equality is necessary but not sufficient. The new predicate requires both equal BCB and `a.span.overlaps_or_adjacent(b.span)`.
Do not require strict overlap only: touching/adjacent spans are eligible for merge; the code says `overlapping or adjacent`.
Do not bridge a hole. The revised pass first discards any covspan overlapping a hole, then refines and merges; the old bucketing behavior is not a license to span across a hole.
Do not restore the old signature extension `fn_sig_span.with_hi(body_span.lo())`; it reintroduces covering the gap between signature and body.
Larger metadata is expected after the fix because there are more distinct spans; do not treat increased raw byte counts or mapping counts as a correctness failure.
Do not rely only on `.coverage` line output: description says reporting changes may be minor or nonexistent even when `.cov-map` metadata changes substantially. Check `.cov-map`/MIR mapping spans.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the existing coverage regression snapshots as focused oracles. In `tests/mir-opt/coverage/instrument_coverage.bar.InstrumentCoverage.diff`, the same `bcb0` must produce separate mappings for the signature, body statement, and closing position rather than one span. In `tests/mir-opt/coverage/branch_match_arms.main.InstrumentCoverage.diff`, equally-BCB spans on lines 14 and 15 must remain separate. In `tests/mir-opt/coverage/instrument_coverage_cleanup.main.CleanupPostBorrowck.diff` and its InstrumentCoverage counterpart, `bcb0` must split into `13:1: 13:10` and `14:8: 14:36` instead of `13:1: 14:36`. Also check `tests/coverage/*.cov-map` snapshots for same-counter mappings that previously spanned comments, blank lines, or macro/attribute gaps, and `tests/coverage/*.coverage` for comments/blank lines changing from counted to uncounted. A focused source pair can use the same function written with a long comment or blank gap between two same-BCB coverage-relevant statements: the corrected metadata keeps multiple same-BCB mappings; the historical transformation would collapse them into one covering the gap. Run through the MIR coverage test harness and snapshot exact spans, not just counts.
